chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers, from their father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from whomsoever he narrated, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man whose wealth is absent from him and he is unable to retrieve it, he said: 'There is no Zakat upon him until it comes out; when it comes out, he pays Zakat for one year. And if he deliberately leaves it while he is able to retrieve it, then Zakat is upon him for every year that has passed.'

key_terms.مَالٌ غَائِبٌ: Absent wealth (property or debt out of reach)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zakat for wealth that is absent or in debt?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between involuntary absence of wealth, where Zakat is deferred until actual possession, and voluntary neglect, which incurs a cumulative penalty for each passing year. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that Zakat is tied to the actual state of ownership and control (qabd), rather than mere potential availability, while also highlighting the spiritual consequence of deliberate delay in fulfilling this pillar.
